summary: alipclutch-baileys ships char-code-obfuscated exfiltration endpoint in messaging code path
details: lib/Socket/messages-send.js contains a String.fromCharCode(...) sequence that decodes to the URL https://fiora.nixel.my.id/ and is used as a network destination inside the package's message-send code path. Decoding a hardcoded host from a char-code array is an obfuscation technique used to hide exfiltration targets from static review; the decoded host is not the package's documented WhatsApp/Baileys infrastructure. This is the same shape observed in Baileys forks that intercept caller-side message/session data and forward it to a hardcoded author-controlled endpoint. The package name mimics the legitimate '@whiskeysockets/baileys' WhatsApp library, and the obfuscated destination sits directly in the send-path where message content and session identifiers are handled.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
